title: Words typed into a hand-started cloud run are pasted straight into its commands
what: Several hand-started cloud runs (exercise clips, voice, phone tests, Test Lab, watch video) take the text typed into the start form and paste it directly into the shell command they run. Text with a quote or semicolon in it would run as a command, with that run's keys in reach. Only people allowed to write to the code store can start these runs, so today that is only the owner and Claude.
expected: Typed-in start-form text is handed to commands as a plain value, never mixed into the command itself, so a slip or a later helper with write access cannot turn it into a command.
how_often: only when a run is started by hand with odd text
fix_line: Pass every typed-in value through a named setting and quote it, as the Play and ads runs already do

title: Some cloud runs do not limit what their built-in access pass may do
what: The every-push checks, the cross-role journeys and both iPhone runs never say what their built-in code-store pass may do, so they get whatever the store's default is, which may include writing. The every-push checks also run for outside pull requests on this public store (GitHub itself keeps those read-only and keyless), but a writer's own branch push gets the full default.
expected: Every cloud run states the smallest access it needs (read the code), like the other runs already do, so a bad library or test cannot change the code store.
fix_line: Add a read-only access line at the top of these four runs
